title: Olivia and the Three Faces of Water
subtitle: Ice, puddle, cloud — same stuff
author: Olivia's Shelf
blurb: Olivia watches an ice cube become a puddle, then a cloud on the window, and learns that water can wear three faces.

magic.launch: The little rocket pushed the air, and the air pushed back.
magic.drop: Everything falls. That pull has a name: gravity.

grok.instructions: Warm, clear storyteller reading a science picture book to a child. Curious, never lecturing. Pause at full stops.

openai.instructions: Warm, clear storyteller reading a science picture book to a child. Curious, never lecturing. Pause at full stops.

pages.heading: Water standing still
pages.text: {Olivia} held an {ice} cube on the {workshop} bench. Hard. Cold. "That is water standing still," said {Elon:elon/look}.

pages.heading: A sliding face
pages.text: The cube became a {puddle} in her palm. "Same water, now sliding," said {Elon:elon/teach}. "{Heat} made it change face."

pages.heading: A flying face
pages.text: The puddle vanished from the warm window. "It did not disappear," said Elon. "It became {air}-water. We call that {steam}."

pages.heading: Faces can turn back
pages.text: Steam on a cold pane turned back into {drops}. "Faces can change both {ways}," said Elon.

pages.heading: Clouds are drops
pages.text: They looked at a {cloud:stars/glow}. "Clouds are tiny drops," said {Elon:elon/teach}. "{Rain} is those drops holding hands and falling."

pages.heading: Keep asking why
pages.text: "Why can water be three things?" asked {Olivia:olivia/ask}. "Its tiny bits can hold, slide, or fly," said {Elon:elon/teach}. "Ask why again tomorrow."

end.heading: The End
end.text: Water can be ice, puddle, or cloud. Same stuff. Three faces.
end.prompt: Where will you look for water's three faces tomorrow?

credits: Painted for Olivia's Shelf. Elon is a picture-book inventor who teaches physics; this is not a biography.

questions.right: That's right. Heat speeds the tiny bits.
Yes. Tiny drops. Rain is those drops falling.
questions.wrong: Clouds are tiny drops of water.
